dominant_breach: strategic-mineral industrial policy can socialize supply-chain risk and revenue costs while private firms retain upside and communities/resource hosts absorb externalities
fastest_washout: tax-expenditure opacity, milestone slippage, local environmental/service costs, subsidy capture, and weak clawback terms wash out claimed public benefit

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: Critical-minerals policy can be public-wealth-positive only if public support buys resilience, shared upside, enforceable domestic/community benefits, and remediation rather than private subsidy capture.

critical_minerals_supply_chain_subsidy_c.note: Supply-chain-security urgency plus grants, loans, tax expenditures, and accelerator funding heightens subsidy-capture risk unless beneficiaries and milestones are named.

industrial_policy_public_upside_recovery.note: Public downside must be paired with warrants/equity, royalties, revenue sharing, clawbacks, domestic-value obligations, price/volume commitments, or enforceable community benefits.

strategic_resource_permitting_community_.note: Strategic permitting must still score resource-host communities, water, labor, environmental remediation, tribal/Indigenous rights, and local service burdens.

supply_chain_security_public_risk_transf.note: Supply-chain shock arguments can transfer risk to the public while private firms retain upside unless offtake, price, and security terms are transparent.

tax_expenditure_hidden_public_balance_sh.note: Energy/industrial tax expenditures must be compared with direct spending, distributional incidence, beneficiary data, sunset, and evaluation metrics.

tax_expenditure_vs_direct_spending_trans.note: Oversight requires data on supported projects, goals, fraud risk, and comparability with direct spending.

public_procurement_capture.note: Procurement or offtake support can become capture if milestone, domestic-value, labor, and public-upside terms are weak.

generational_incidence.note: Long-lived subsidy, supply-chain, environmental, and revenue choices can shift costs or benefits across cohorts and regions.

proof_debt: project-level tax expenditure, grant, loan, procurement, offtake, and beneficiary data
public-upside recovery terms: equity, warrants, royalties, revenue sharing, clawbacks, domestic-value obligations, or price/volume commitments
community benefit, labor, environmental, water, tribal/Indigenous/local consent, and remediation protections
supply-chain concentration, export-control, processing/refining bottleneck, and offtake dependency stress test
direct-spending versus tax-expenditure comparison, with non-awardees and harmed communities included as claimants

gate_06_wealth_to_rule_capture.why: Strategic-sector urgency can produce capture if subsidy recipients help define weak accountability rules.

gate_07_public_common_counterweight.why: Industrial policy counts as public counterweight only when public value and claimant protection are durable.

gate_15_place_public_finance.why: Resource-host communities and local infrastructure bear siting/permitting/service costs.

gate_20_public_balance_sheet.why: Comfort certification is blocked until project-level public support, public-upside recovery, community burden, supply-chain security, and direct-spending comparators are transparent and enforceable.

evidence_debt_register.question: project-level public support and beneficiary map
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Attach grants, loans, tax credits, procurement/offtake, DPA/DOE program awards, ownership, and expected public purpose by project.

evidence_debt_register.question: public-upside and clawback terms
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Require warrants/equity, royalties, revenue sharing, clawbacks, domestic-value obligations, price/volume commitments, or enforceable community benefits.

evidence_debt_register.question: community/environmental and host-claimant incidence
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Score water, remediation, labor, tribal/local consent, infrastructure, and long-term environmental liabilities.

evidence_debt_register.question: supply-chain security stress test
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Test concentration, processing/refining bottlenecks, export controls, and offtake dependency against public support terms.

validation_notes: rev0320 treats strategic industrial policy as potentially public-wealth-positive but only after subsidy capture, tax-expenditure opacity, community burden, and public-upside recovery are scored.

rev0327 promotes this scoreboard to active: DOE funding/current industrial-policy evidence lets the cube score public-upside recovery and subsidy-capture risk now, while project-level beneficiary ledgers remain proof debt.

public_balance_sheet_register.exposure_name: Critical-minerals industrial-policy subsidy, tax-expenditure, and supply-chain backstop
public_balance_sheet_register.legal_authority: DOE critical-minerals programs, federal tax expenditures, procurement/offtake commitments, loans/loan guarantees, Defense Production Act-style authorities where applicable, permitting and environmental law, and state/local economic-development agreements.
public_balance_sheet_register.claimant_perimeter: Mining/refining/recycling firms, battery and clean-tech manufacturers, workers, local/resource-host communities, Indigenous and environmental claimants, taxpayers, consumers, and strategic-security agencies
public_balance_sheet_register.maximum_exposure: Unknown without program-by-program subsidy, tax expenditure, loan, guarantee, procurement, and permitting registers; energy tax expenditures alone are a large foregone-revenue channel
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Unknown; expected public cost depends on utilization, fraud risk, milestone compliance, market prices, supply-chain concentration, and clawback/enforcement strength
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: A supply-chain-security shock or industrial-policy race accelerates critical-minerals support; public grants, tax expenditures, loans, or procurement reduce private risk while local communities and future taxpayers absorb cost, remediation, and underperformance.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: foregone federal revenue, grants, public loans/guarantees, procurement/offtake contracts, state/local incentives, infrastructure spending, and environmental/public-service budgets
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Private developers, sponsors, offtakers, and processors should absorb first loss through matching capital, clawbacks, milestone forfeiture, completion guarantees, remediation bonds, and enforceable domestic/community obligations.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Equity/warrants, royalties, revenue sharing, price/volume commitments, domestic processing obligations, clawbacks, public IP/licensing rights, community benefit agreements, and remediation bonds.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: Protect taxpayers, workers, local/resource-host communities, Indigenous claimants, and consumers from subsidy capture, environmental loss, and weak supply-chain security outcomes
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Award/milestone review, annual tax-expenditure evaluation, supply-chain stress refresh, and event-triggered review after export-control, closure, default, environmental, or community-claim event.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Strategic supply-chain beneficiaries and project sponsors
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Often first recipients of subsidy/credit/procurement support
seniority_waterfall.notes: Strategic urgency can move private firms to the front of the public-risk line.
Tax expenditures are hidden public-balance-sheet commitments unless compared to direct spending.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Resource-host communities, workers, and environmental/Indigenous claimants
seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Often conditionally protected through permitting or benefit agreements
seniority_waterfall.notes: Protection must be enforceable and funded before extraction or processing begins.

seniority_waterfall.claimant: Future energy-system users and future taxpayers
seniority_waterfall.notes: They inherit either resilient supply chains or failed subsidy, environmental, and concentration risks.
